rules.title: Notice required to terminate a tenancy at will
rules.requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months. If rent is payable more often than every three months, notice equal to the rent interval or thirty days, whichever is longer, is enough. The notice may include an offer of a new tenancy on different terms without becoming invalid.
rules.key_value: Rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer (max 3 months)
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenancies at will in Massachusetts; applies to both landlord and tenant.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to tenancies at will, not fixed-term leases

rules.quoted_span: Section 12. Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.
rules.conflict_note: This is an eviction-procedure notice rule, not a just-cause requirement. The document gives no effective date.

rules.title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment and tenant right to cure
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end a tenancy at will with a 14-day written notice to quit. A tenant who has not received a similar notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days of receiving the notice. The notice must include the statutory right-to-cure notification; if it is missing, the cure period runs until the answer date in the possession action.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies at will in Massachusetts where the tenant has failed or refused to pay rent.
rules.exemptions: No right to cure if the tenant received a similar nonpayment notice within the preceding 12 months.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to tenancies at will; the right to cure depends on whether a prior notice was given within 12 months

rules.penalty: If the notice omits the required notification, the tenant's cure period extends to the day the answer is due in the landlord's possession action.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.
rules.conflict_note: The document gives no effective date.

rules.title: Continuance when nonpayment is caused by government payment delay
rules.requirement: If nonpayment was caused by a government failure or delay in delivering a subsistence or rental payment, the court must continue the possession hearing at least seven days. If all rent due, with interest and costs, is tendered within that time, the tenancy is treated as not terminated.
rules.coverage_conditions: Possession actions for nonpayment of rent where the nonpayment resulted from a federal, state or municipal agency's failure or delay in mailing or delivering a non-salary subsistence or rental payment.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where nonpayment was caused by a government payment or voucher delay

rules.quoted_span: If the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality, or any departments, agencies or authorities thereof, in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment to either the tenant or the landlord, the court in any action for possession shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.
rules.conflict_note: The document gives no effective date.
